easy.explanation: Isaiah calls them “the drunkards of Ephraim.”
easy.q: How are the people of Ephraim described in verse 1?

answers: It will be trodden under feet
easy.explanation: The passage says, “The crown of pride… shall be trodden under feet.”
easy.q: What will happen to Ephraim's crown of pride?

easy.explanation: Its glorious beauty is described as “a fading flower.”
easy.q: What is Ephraim's glorious beauty compared to?

answers: It will become stronger with time
medium.explanation: The hasty fruit is eaten as soon as it is seen and held, suggesting a swift end.
medium.q: What does the image of the hasty fruit suggest about Ephraim's glory?

answers: A place of richness and pleasure
medium.explanation: The fat valleys are associated with Ephraim's beauty, abundance, and pride.
medium.q: What does “the fat valleys” suggest in this passage?

answers: A storm of hail and mighty waters
medium.explanation: The Lord is described as bringing a tempest of hail and overflowing mighty waters.
medium.q: What brings down Ephraim's glory according to the passage?

answers: Outward glory contrasted with imminent ruin
challenge.explanation: Ephraim appears glorious, but its beauty is already fading and will be trampled.
challenge.q: What is the main contrast in Isaiah's description of Ephraim?

answers: A flower is beautiful but temporary
challenge.explanation: The fading flower represents beauty and splendor that do not last.
challenge.q: Why is the image of a fading flower especially fitting for Ephraim's pride?

answers: Drunkenness represents lost judgment within their pride
challenge.explanation: Though they are proud, the people are overcome with wine and unable to recognize their danger.
challenge.q: What connection does the passage make between drunkenness and pride?

paragraphs.title: The Lord as Glory and Justice, Yet Jerusalem Is Also Drunk

easy.explanation: The Lord will be a crown and diadem “unto the residue of his people.”
easy.q: To whom will the Lord be a crown of glory and a diadem of beauty?

easy.explanation: Isaiah specifically says, “the priest and the prophet have erred through strong drink.”
easy.q: Who are said to have erred through wine and strong drink?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “all tables are full of vomit and filthiness.”

medium.explanation: The Lord will be “a spirit of judgment to him that sitteth in judgment.”
medium.q: What will the Lord be to the one who sits in judgment?

medium.explanation: A diadem is a crown, fitting the verse's language of glory and beauty.
medium.q: In this context, what does “diadem” mean?

answers: They refused to hear the teaching
medium.explanation: The Lord offered rest and refreshing, but “they would not hear,” so the word became a snare.
medium.q: Why did the word of the Lord become a stumbling block to the people?

answers: The Lord is glory and judgment to the residue, while the leaders are described as drunk
Both groups are described as farmers
Both groups reject every word of the Lord
challenge.explanation: The passage contrasts the Lord's blessing on the residue with the leaders' drunken confusion.
challenge.q: What contrast appears between the residue of the people and the priest and prophet?

answers: A measured teaching that the people reject
A plan for building the temple
challenge.explanation: The repeated phrases present instruction given carefully and progressively, though the people refuse to hear it.
challenge.q: What does the repetition of “precept upon precept” and “line upon line” suggest?

answers: Drunkenness causes confusion and error in judgment
challenge.explanation: The priest and prophet are said to err in vision and stumble in judgment because of strong drink.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between drunkenness and unjust judgment in the passage?

paragraphs.title: False Refuge and the Firm Stone in Zion

easy.explanation: Isaiah calls them “scornful men, that rule this people.”
easy.q: How are the rulers of Jerusalem addressed at the beginning of the passage?

easy.explanation: They said, “we have made lies our refuge, and under falsehood have we hid ourselves.”
easy.q: What did the rulers make their refuge?

easy.explanation: The Lord laid in Zion “a foundation, a stone, a tried stone, a precious corner stone.”
easy.q: What did the Lord lay in Zion?

medium.explanation: The Lord will lay judgment to the line and righteousness to the plummet, sweeping away the false refuge.
medium.q: What will expose the refuge of lies?

answers: A stone used only for decoration
medium.explanation: The tried stone and sure foundation symbolize reliable truth and security established by God.
medium.q: What does the “tried stone” represent in the passage?

answers: The hail and waters will sweep it away
medium.explanation: The hail will sweep away the refuge of lies, and the waters will overflow the hiding place.
medium.q: What will happen to the rulers' false security?

answers: The rulers trust in lies, while the Lord establishes a true foundation
The rulers trust in Zion, while the Lord establishes a lie
Both images describe the same kind of security
challenge.explanation: The covenant with death represents false security, while the stone represents God's sure foundation.
challenge.q: What is the meaning of the contrast between the covenant with death and the stone in Zion?

answers: Continued mockery may bring a stronger and more certain judgment
Mockery is welcomed by the Lord
The rulers have already corrected their ways
challenge.explanation: Isaiah warns that continued mockery will make their bands strong and bring determined destruction.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the warning, “be ye not mockers”?

answers: One who trusts the true foundation is not driven into panic
The believer hides himself in falsehood
challenge.explanation: The sure foundation represents stability, so the believer does not need to flee in fear.
challenge.q: Why does “he that believeth shall not make haste” fit the image of the sure foundation?

paragraphs.title: The Farmer's Parable: Wisdom, Order, and Measure

answers: He prepares and breaks up the ground
easy.explanation: The plowman opens and breaks the clods of the ground before sowing.
easy.q: What does the plowman do before sowing?

easy.explanation: The passage mentions casting abroad the fitches and scattering the cummin.
easy.q: Which seeds are mentioned in the parable?

answers: It is not continued without limit
It is always done in exactly the same way
easy.explanation: The passage says that bread corn is not threshed forever and that different plants require different methods.
easy.q: What does the parable teach about threshing?

medium.explanation: The farmer first prepares the soil, then sows the seed, and finally processes the harvest.
medium.q: What is the main order of actions in the farmer's parable?

answers: A tool used to separate grain
medium.explanation: A threshing instrument is used to process grain, but the fitches are beaten with a staff instead.
medium.q: What does “a threshing instrument” refer to in this passage?

medium.explanation: The fitches, cummin, and bread corn are handled differently according to their nature.
medium.q: Why are different methods used for different plants?

answers: Wisdom follows order, suitability, and measure
challenge.explanation: The farmer knows when to plow, what to sow, and how to treat each crop.
challenge.q: What central idea does the farmer's parable teach about wisdom?

answers: As the farmer follows an appointed order, people should recognize God's instruction
God's laws are merely descriptions of farming
challenge.explanation: The parable shows that God's wisdom establishes proper order and limits that should not be resisted.
challenge.q: How does the farmer's parable relate to human obedience to God's ways?

answers: Correction and judgment also have proper limits and measure
Everything should be threshed until destroyed
The result of work has no importance
challenge.explanation: The passage emphasizes that threshing has a purpose and a limit, illustrating wise and measured action.
challenge.q: What can be learned from the fact that the farmer does not thresh forever?
